{{Top}}
{{Quote|Word of warning - watch your step, or you'll fall for hours.|[[Atton Rand]], referring to the heights of Nar Shaddaa|<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Coruscant_landscape_TPM.png|thumb|300px|The cityscape of Coruscant, the most famous and prominent ecumenopolis]]
An '''ecumenopolis''' was a type of [[Planet/Legends|planet]], or in some cases a [[Moon/Legends|moon]], whose entire surface was covered with a single worldwide [[City/Legends|city]].

==History==
[[File:Coruscant_at_night.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The ecumenopolis of Coruscant]]
The [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Species/Legends|species]] had become advanced enough to transform [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] into an ecumenopolis as early as a [[100,000 BBY/Legends|hundred thousand]] years prior to the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. By [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]], [[Taris/Legends|Taris]] became one, having built itself up during the course of only a single century of prosperity; this world, however, still had its [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]], meaning only its landmasses had been completely built over.

One example of a lunar ecumenopolis was [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], the largest moon that orbited the adopted homeworld of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]], [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]]. As far back as the [[Jedi Civil War]] and possibly long before, it had become entirely covered in [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]]-tall buildings, many of the lower areas of which had become quite decayed.

==Ecumenopolises in the galaxy==
[[File:Nar_Shaddaa_DE.jpg|thumb|180px|A district on Nar Shaddaa]]
There were many ecumenopolises within [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], most notably:

==Behind the scenes==
"Ecumenopolis" comes from the [[Wikipedia:Greek language|Greek]] "οικουμένη" (oecumen) meaning "world," and "πόλις" (polis) meaning "city," thus translating to "world-city, a city made of the whole world." The term was coined in 1967 by the Greek city planner [[Wikipedia:Constantinos Doxiadis|Constantinos Doxiadis]].<ref name="Doxiadis">{{WebCite|url=http://www.doxiadis.org/page/default.asp?id=238|text=Ecumenopolis: Tomorrow's City|work=Constantinos A. Doxiadis|archivedate=20120207010635}}</ref><!-- ORIGINAL: <ref name="Doxiadis">{{WebCite|url=http://www.doxiadis.org/page/default.asp?id=238|text=Ecumenopolis: Tomorrow's City|work=Constantinos A. Doxiadis|archivedate=20120207010635}}</ref> --> The term made its first appearance in a ''[[Star Wars]]'' source in ''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]''.

The game ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]'' incorrectly depicts [[Corulag/Legends|Corulag]] as an ecumenopolis; however, the only depiction of it as such is in its land map (which is a single cityscape), and that map may take place in the only large city on Corulag. Similarly, [[Kuat/Legends|Kuat]] is described as covered in city-sprawl in ''[[Rules of Engagement: The Rebel SpecForce Handbook]]'', though later sources have shown that the planet did in fact remain fairly free of urban sprawl, with the planet's industrialization being in the form of its massive orbital facilities.
